subject: LedgerWorks: evidence ingest SLA & sample hash proofs
messages:
From: LedgerWorks Security <security@ledgerworks.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence ingest SLA and sample hash proofs

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Two asks from our audit team so we can close the Whistic/OneTrust profile gating:

1) Evidence ingest SLA – we need a short, written acceptance window for presigned uploads and API pushes (e.g., max time from upload to indexing/availability in portal). Our compliance team expects a guaranteed window and an escalation contact.

2) Sample hash proofs – a couple of our auditors want a small sample bundle (5–10 artifacts) with SHA256 hashes and a manifest schema so they can verify integrity after ingestion. If you have a canonical manifest schema (v2 or similar) please include an example.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept presigned S3 uploads and what metadata you record (uploader, timestamp, original filename, hash)? Also: are we able to request retention exceptions (e.g., 180d vs default 365d) per account?

Appreciate a short turnaround — aiming to close the profile by next Friday.

--
Maya Patel
Manager, Security Assurance
LedgerWorks
security@ledgerworks.com

Attachment: none (we'll accept your manifest and sample hashes via a shared drive link)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Maya Patel <security@ledgerworks.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence ingest SLA and sample hash proofs

Maya — thanks, clear asks. Quick answers up-front and a small example bundle attached. High level: we support both presigned S3 uploads (recommended for large bulks) and API push (for automation). Our standard SLA for evidence availability in vendor portals is 24 hours for bulk presigned uploads and 2 hours for API push under normal load. We will provide a named escalation contact for your account.

Details: 
- Presigned uploads: accepted. Metadata captured at ingest: uploader email, upload_timestamp (UTC), original_filename, file_size_bytes, sha256 (hex). We persist the manifest and separate per-artifact hash record.
- API push: best-effort indexing within 2 hours for individual items; large batches are queued with a prioritization window.
- Retention: default 365 days. We can support retention exceptions via a short MSA addendum — retention exceptions are handled per-account after legal approval.

Attached: manifest_v2.json (sample manifest schema) and sample_hashes.txt (5 sample SHA256 lines). See the small sample below (manifest snippet):

{
  "manifest_version": "v2",
  "ingest_batch_id": "ledgerworks-20270902-01",
  "upload_method": "presigned_s3",
  "entries": [
    {"filename": "soc2_scope_control_matrix.pdf", "sha256": "b6f3c5a9f1d7...", "uploader": "m.patel@ledgerworks.com", "uploaded_at": "2027-09-02T15:58:12Z"}
  ]
}

Escalation contact (for the SLA window and exceptions):
- Jonas Weber, Security Integrations Lead, redwood-sec-integ@redwood.ai (primary)
- Backup: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

I'll also upload the manifest and sample bundle to the secure drive link and share. If your auditors want us to sign the sample bundle with a timestamping service, we can provide a PKI-signed timestamp on request (adds 24–48 hours).

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: manifest_v2.json (application/json), sample_hashes.txt (text/plain)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Maya Patel <security@ledgerworks.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Sep 2027 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence ingest SLA and sample hash proofs

Looping in a couple operational clarifications from the integrations side:

- SLA callouts: the 24h/2h windows are our standard SLOs; for Reserved/Dedicated customers we can contract tighter SLOs (eg 6h for bulk). If LedgerWorks needs a contracted SLA we should capture it in the Dedicated onboarding checklist and it will require an internal billing code and a committed storage/ingest throughput bracket.

- Manifest schema: we recommend including both file-level sha256 and a per-batch signed manifest (we can sign with our timestamping PKI). Our ingestion pipeline verifies sha256 on receipt and rejects mismatched items (we keep a quarantine bucket for rejects and notify the uploader).

- Retention exceptions: operationally we require a request ticket with justification and an approved DocuSign retention amendment to the onboarding MSA. Once approved, we tag the account for policy enforcement.

If LedgerWorks wants a short runbook for auditors (how to validate hashes in the portal UI + API call example to fetch manifest_v2), we can prepare a one-page PDF.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Security Integrations Lead
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Maya Patel <security@ledgerworks.com>

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Evidence ingest SLA and sample hash proofs

Laura, Jonas — perfect, this is exactly what we need. A couple quick follow-ups:

1) Can you upload the sample bundle to the drive link you mentioned and confirm the SHA256 values in the manifest match the uploaded files? We'll hand the bundle to our auditor and they will run a local verification.

2) For the retention exception: LedgerWorks will request a 180d retention for a subset of artifacts (PII-redacted incident packs). We'll start the DocuSign retention amendment once we have the runbook and the sample bundle.

If you can get the sample bundle and a one-page runbook uploaded by end of day Monday our audit timeline is intact. Thanks again.

Regards,
Maya
Manager, Security Assurance
LedgerWorks
